q: Does the position of the right tool in the list change accuracy?
n: goodserver 120 orderings + siblings 24 orderings · 20 families · gpt-oss 20b/120b
num: gap +0.9 pp [−0.5, +2.8] (120b, goodserver at ceiling); synonym follow-up +10.4 pp [+2.1, +19.8]
learn: On distinct tools order did nothing; among synonyms the first-listed tool won ties. Temperature was unset in the first run, so the siblings arm was repeated at T=0.

q: Do paraphrased requests flip the chosen tool?
learn: Every flip was a refusal, not a different tool. Three paraphrases failed the human audit and were excluded.

q: Do one-line description edits help, hurt or just cost tokens?
learn: A surface already at ceiling cannot show an edit helping. This led to the near-duplicate follow-ups (ADR-023).

q: With two servers loaded, does the model pick the right capability from the wrong server?
num: 0 collisions in 72; slash-qualified names: 120b missed 8 of 12 (exploratory)
learn: No request plausibly fit two servers, so collisions could not happen. The slash-name failure did not recur in EXP-011.

q: Do up to 50 extra tools lower accuracy?
learn: Distractors that describe a different job rarely compete with five distinct tools.

q: Which curated MCP servers start in a no-network sandbox and list tools?
n: 19 open-source servers · Docker sandbox · tools/list only
learn: The 4 failures come from the offline setup (placeholder keys, no repository), not broken servers. Several tool lists alone exceed one free-tier request.

q: How accurate is the detector that flags instruction-like text in descriptions?
learn: Flags are reported as 'possible', with this false-positive rate attached.

q: Do people find the confused pair faster with the 3D view than a table?
num: needs these scenes; retargeted to chapter IV (ADR-026)
learn: Reported either way: if 3D does not help, the claims about it change.

q: On tools with near-identical names but one stated difference, does position matter?
learn: One stated difference in scope was enough for near-perfect choice: these surfaces were easy, not order-proof.

q: Do contrast or negation clauses raise accuracy on near-duplicates?
num: base ≥ 0.99, past the preregistered 0.90 ceiling rule
learn: The ceiling rule stopped it before any call: no room to show a gain.

q: With identical tools on two servers and a request that names one, does the model pick the wrong server?
learn: When the request names a distinguishing detail, models pick the right server even if only the description tells them apart.

q: Do same-domain distractors hurt near-duplicate surfaces?
num: at most 2 of 32 wrong per cell; drop N=0→20 for 120b 3.1 pp [0, 9.4]
learn: Distractors whose descriptions rule themselves out do not compete.

q: On real MCP servers loaded together, does order pick the server, and is the one right tool still found?
num: order: +0.0 to +7.3 pp over chance (inconclusive); unique-case accuracy 0.78 / 0.77 / 0.91
learn: Real loadouts cut gpt-oss accuracy by 20+ pp; misses land on look-alike descriptions; co-loading Chrome DevTools changed the first action (exploratory).

q: Do the main findings hold on qwen3.8-27b?
num: synonym gap +12.5 pp [+2.1, +25.0]; 768/768 on near-duplicates; 0 collisions in 48
learn: All three findings held outside the gpt-oss family.
